Subject: Evaluation plan + acceptance criteria (pilot)

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team liked how Redwood handled latency spikes and the KV cache behavior. We're ready to run a short pilot but procurement needs a clear evaluation plan and measurable acceptance tests so legal/procurement can sign off. High-level asks below:

- Primary success criteria:
  - Latency: p95 end-to-end < 400ms for our 1k-token prompts under expected load (see load profile in attachment).
  - Throughput: sustain 50 req/s concurrent with 100ms mean model decode time (approx).
  - Quality: entity extraction recall >= 0.92 on our 200-sample gold set, and hallucination rate < 3% on test prompts.
  - Security/compliance: SOC2 evidence, audit log access, and keys managed by our KMS (we require explicit data retention policy).

- Exit gates we care about: security signoff, performance gates met in three runbooked test cases, and a PO/procurement milestone within 30 days of pilot finish.

I've attached a short spreadsheet with our goals and a sample prompt set (CuraTech-Eval-Goals.xlsx). Can you propose an evaluation plan and mutual action path (MAP) with owners and dates? We need this to move to procurement.

Thanks,
Emma Clarke
Head of AI Strategy
CuraTech

Hi Emma — great to hear you're ready to move forward. Attached is a draft MAP (Redwood_MAP_v1.xlsx) and a short proposed timeline. High level: 3 phases (Discovery, Pilot, Decision) with clear exit gates and acceptance tests for each phase. Summary below — please confirm owners and whether the dates look OK.

Proposed MAP summary (week-of dates in PST):
- Discovery (Dec 6–10) — owners: Vanessa (redwood AE), Emma (curatech PM)
  - Deliverables: integration checklist, sample data handoff, baseline quality run on 200 samples.
  - Exit gate: integration complete and baseline recall/precision captured.

- Pilot (Dec 13–26) — owners: Dev Patel (SE), CuraTech infra lead
  - Acceptance tests: 1) Load/perf test at 50 req/s (p95 < 400ms), 2) Quality test vs gold set (recall >= 0.92), 3) Security smoke (KMS + audit logs verified). Runbook will include exact test scripts.
  - Exit gate: all three acceptance tests marked PASS in runbook.

- Decision window / Close (Dec 27–Jan 7) — owners: Vanessa, Marcus Lin (sales manager), CuraTech procurement
  - Deliverables: Procurement PO, SOW signature, production rollout plan.

Open asks for you:
1) Confirm procurement contact and target PO date (you mentioned 30 days after pilot end — is Dec 31 achievable?).
2) Confirm sample set & we will schedule pilot kickoff on Dec 8 if that works.

I've attached the MAP draft and labeled the acceptance tests. We'll update the file to include your procurement timeline once you confirm.

Thanks, Vanessa — adding a technical acceptance checklist for the pilot tests. I've attached a PDF with test cases and pass/fail criteria. Quick highlights and test scaffolding below.

Technical acceptance checklist (high level):
- Integration tests (owner: CuraTech infra + Redwood SE)
  - API integration: sample payloads processed end-to-end, payload schema validated.
  - KV cache behavior test: verify session continuity across 10 concurrent clients.

- Performance tests (owner: Redwood SE)
  - Synthetic load: ramp to 50 req/s sustained for 10 minutes; measure p50/p95/p99. Pass if p95 < 400ms.
  - Spike resilience: run short spikes to 150 req/s and confirm graceful shedding/fallback within SLO.

- Quality tests (owner: CuraTech data lead + Redwood SE)
  - Run the 200-sample gold set through the exact prompt templates; compute recall/precision. Pass if recall >= 0.92 and hallucination rate <3%.
  - Regression checks: compare to baseline from Discovery.

- Security & compliance checks (owner: CuraTech security + Redwood security)
  - KMS integration: keys rotate and access logs visible to CuraTech.
  - Audit log sampling: export and verify for 48 hours of pilot traffic.
  - Data retention: confirm ephemeral cache behavior and documented retention period.

- Failure & rollback scenarios
  - Simulate a model fallback and verify response formats/latency expectations.
  - Automated alerting verifies triggers at 95th percentile breach.
